title: The eighth: Mina
hook: pilgrims go to Mina, a city of tents

segments.voice: Yesterday: sa'y, seven lengths between Safa and Marwa in Hajar's footsteps. Your line: in her footsteps.

On the eighth day, where did the Prophet pray the noon prayer? Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay wanted a straight answer, so he asked Anas ibn Malik, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: tell me something you remember. Anas answered: at Mina. The exchange is in Sahih al-Bukhari, and it's how the days of Hajj itself begin. Not at the Ka'ba. Outside the city, in a valley of tents. Today, the eighth.
screen: `WHERE DID HE PRAY AT NOON?` → `AT MINA.` → `A VALLEY OF TENTS.`

segments.voice: First, the date. The circling and the walking can be done at other times of year too. Hajj proper has its own days in the month of Dhul-Hijjah, and in Jabir's account they begin on the eighth, the day of tarwiyah. Pilgrims who have come out of ihram enter it again, and the crowd moves out of Mecca to Mina. Second, what the Prophet did there. Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says that on that day they set out for Mina, and the Prophet prayed there the noon, afternoon, sunset, evening and dawn prayers. Then he waited a little until the sun had risen, and went on. That's the whole of the eighth: travel, five prayers, one night, and waiting. No great ritual. A pause before Arafah. Third, the place now. Mina today is a valley filled with row after row of tents, white and fireproof, set up for the days of Hajj and almost empty the rest of the year. People from far and wide sleep side by side on thin mattresses, share food, queue for the washrooms, and pray together on carpets laid over the ground. The surgeon in white cloth from a week ago now shares a tent with strangers. Fourth, the end of Anas's answer. He closed with a line: do as your leaders do. Pilgrims follow the group, move when it moves, rest when it rests. The Qur'an, in surah two, speaks of the days spent here later in the Hajj; in Pickthall's words: "Remember Allah through the appointed days." A city of tents is made for exactly that: not much to do, and plenty of time to remember.
screen: `THE FIRST DAY OF HAJJ PROPER.` · `FIVE PRAYERS AND ONE NIGHT.` · `STRANGERS SIDE BY SIDE.` · `DO AS YOUR LEADERS DO.`

segments.voice: Sit somewhere snug, a corner of a room, the edge of a bed, a parked car, with nothing to do, and notice how close the walls are and how little you need. If you pray, use the time for remembrance, a few words of praise you know, said slowly; if not, stay with the breath and the smallness of the space.
The eighth. The eighth of Dhul-Hijjah, when pilgrims go out to Mina, pray, and spend the night in tents. Today's word.
Your line: a city of tents. Strangers side by side, with time to remember. Same time tomorrow.

notes: Bukhari 1653 (Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay asks Anas where the Prophet prayed zuhr on the day of tarwiyah: 'at Mina'; then 'do as your leaders do', which in the report concerns where to pray asr on the day of departure): confirm number, and that the summary of 'do as your leaders do' is fair.
Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir: on the day of tarwiyah they went to Mina; the Prophet prayed zuhr, asr, maghrib, isha and fajr there, waited until sunrise): confirm.
Pickthall 2:203 quoted from memory: confirm. The verse is generally read as the days of tashriq at Mina after the day of sacrifice; the script says 'later in the Hajj'.
Description of modern Mina (white fireproof tents, nearly empty outside Hajj, people from far and wide): general color; confirm.
'Hajj proper has its own days ... the eighth is the first of them': standard description; confirm phrasing.
